properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-26, thinking out loud: *"what are some things we can do to increase the probability that an agent will use reflow2 skills and tools in a project? what would make the agent say, I have the perfect skill or tool needed for problem X? hopefully, by adding depth and layers, we can start seeing much more clearly why and when some skills/tools are used."*

**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Nothing here is decided; the options are put down so a later session meets the reasoning rather than re-deriving it.

═══ THE FRAME BEING PROPOSED: FOUR LAYERS, AND A SKIP HAPPENS AT THE WEAKEST ONE ═══

For an agent to use a skill, four things must all hold. They fail independently, they want different fixes, and reflow2 has not worked them equally:

① **KNOWN** — the agent is aware the thing exists. *(Worked: `list_skills`, `get_skill`, served-not-installed, the handshake catalogue, 24 slash commands.)*

② **RECOGNISED** — the agent notices THIS MOMENT is that skill's moment. *(Worked hard: `cap:skill-triggers`, the three-event loop nudge, `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue`.)*

③ **WORTH IT** — the agent believes the skill beats what it would do unaided. *(BARELY WORKED AT ALL. There is no node arguing that a skill produces a better answer than competent improvisation; the whole surface argues that skipping is non-compliant, which is a different claim and a weaker motivator for something that is not trying to comply.)*

④ **VISIBLE** — something can see whether it happened. *(PARTLY BUILT — see the correction below.)*

⚠️ **CORRECTION MADE IN THE SAME SESSION, AND THE MISTAKE IS WORTH KEEPING.** This node first asserted that layer ④ was DEFERRED, reasoning from `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`, which says so in its own text. That was true when that requirement was written and is now FALSE: `req:skill-adherence-is-measured` is **`accepted`**, and `cap:skill-loads-are-counted` is **built and `verified`**.

**The error is the one this project keeps recording: reading a claim out of one node's prose instead of the node it is about.**

**What layer ④ actually holds now:** skill LOADS are counted, and their absence is announced at session end. **What it still does not hold:** any notion of which skill SHOULD have been loaded for the work that was done.

═══ THE EVIDENCE THAT ③ IS THE BOTTLENECK ═══

`req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` records the same failure twice, six days apart, and the second is the damning one: **`cap:skill-triggers` was `verified` and firing correctly, and the user still had to be the reminder.** Layer ② was WORKING and it was not enough.

It also names the structural ceiling on ②: every shape that capability recognises is a shape in the GRAPH-WRITE stream, so it requires the agent to have already touched the graph. *A skill load is not a graph write.* No amount of work on ② reaches an agent that never started.

⭐ AND THE MEASUREMENT MOST WORTH REPEATING: both observations were made on sessions with **more** context about reflow2 than any consumer's agent will ever have. That is a BEST case, not a typical one.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) Attack layer ③ directly: make the skill's ADVANTAGE legible at the moment of choice.** ⚠️ Counter: self-promotion inside a tool result, and it cannot be honest without evidence.

**(b) Keep hardening ② and accept the ceiling.** ⚠️ Counter: measured twice as insufficient, and the ceiling is structural.

**(c) Finish layer ④ — the half that is missing.** ⚠️ Counter: `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` may forbid the obvious implementation, and that must be settled BEFORE anything is built.

**(d) Reject the frame.** Perhaps the real variable is CONTEXT BUDGET: a skill costs tokens to load mid-task, and an agent under pressure economises. **Nothing has tested this, and it would explain the measured facts as well as ③ does.**

═══ WHY THE FRAME MIGHT EARN ITS KEEP ═══

It gives every future idea a place to attach: a proposal that improves ① when the bottleneck is ③ can be recognised as such before it is built. **It is a diagnostic, not a design.**

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
═══ 📌 SHARPENED 2026-08-26 BY A USER REPORT — AND THE FRAME HAS A HOLE ═══

*A user reported, relayed, that they were "probably not understanding all the skills in reflow2". Recorded here rather than as a new node because this node's own rationale says splitting would "lose the comparison, which is the only part that does any work". Written without the user's domain or employer; the design record is public.*

⭐ **EVERY ONE OF THE FOUR LAYERS IS ABOUT THE AGENT. NONE IS ABOUT THE PERSON.** The frame reads "for an AGENT to use a skill, four things must hold" — and a human who does not know what reflow2 is FOR fails before layer ① is reached. That is a candidate **layer ⓪ — ORIENTED: the person knows what this tool does and what it will ask of them.**

Whether ⓪ belongs in the frame is the open part. Two readings, and they lead to different work:

- **⓪ IS REAL.** reflow2 asks the human questions — gaps, decisions, who they are. A user who cannot answer *"what is this for?"* cannot answer those either, and no amount of agent-side triggering helps.
- **⓪ IS A MIRAGE, and the report is really ① or ③ seen from the user's chair.** reflow2 is AGENT-DRIVEN. The user never picks a skill; they see the consequence of the agent picking one. *"I do not understand the skills"* may be *"the agent never reached for one, and I noticed."* **Then a tutorial teaches the wrong party.**

🛑 **NOTHING WE HAVE DISTINGUISHES THESE**, and that is the same hole layer ④ already names: loads are counted, but not whether the RIGHT skill was owed. `dec:bl-155`'s warning applies exactly — it could not tell *unused* from *unreachable*, and this cannot tell *uninformed user* from *unreaching agent*.

📌 **WHAT IS ACTUALLY MEASURED TODAY, so ① is not overstated:** 22 served skills, 163 tools, `list_skills` / `get_skill` / `find_tools`, `docs/skills-and-tools.md`, 24 slash commands. All answer *"what is there?"*. **None answers *"where do I start?"*** — `genesis` covers a new PROJECT, `adopt` covers existing CODE, and nothing covers a new PERSON.

⭐ **AND A WORKED EXAMPLE OF THE FRAME FAILING BELOW ALL FOUR LAYERS**, measured the same day: `fact:the-lens-that-carries-the-persona-was-built-on-a-branch-and-never-shipped`. The mechanism that would carry a reader's background to the agent was built, core-tested, and left on an unmerged branch. That is not ①, ②, ③ or ④ — the thing was never in the surface at all, while the design recorded the capability as existing. **A fifth failure mode: the mechanism is in the DESIGN and not in the BUILD.** Whether the frame should carry that too, or whether it belongs to release hygiene rather than adoption, is unsettled.

⚠️ **THE COUNTERWEIGHT ON ALL OF IT:** n=1, relayed, from a user who cannot share specifics. This project's own history says the tempting fix is the wrong one. Before building a guide, the honest step is the one `report_manual_work` now exists to catch — get the case in the user's own words, and find out whether they wanted a skill they could not find or never knew a skill was owed.
properties.name: OPEN — an agent skips a skill at one of four layers, and a fifth may sit under them: which is reflow2's real bottleneck?
properties.rationale:
Recorded as one Decision because it is one question — WHERE does the failure live — and the layers are its options rather than separate questions. Splitting it would lose the comparison, which is the only part that does any work.

The counter-argument to the frame itself is written in as option (d) rather than left out, because a frame that cannot be wrong is not a diagnostic.

SHARPENED 2026-08-26. A user report about not understanding the skills was recorded HERE rather than as a parallel node, on that same reasoning. It contributes two things the frame did not have: a candidate layer ⓪ (the PERSON, where all four existing layers are about the AGENT), and a worked example of a failure that sits below all of them — a mechanism present in the design and absent from the build. Both are offered as questions about the frame rather than as extensions of it, because a diagnostic that grows a layer every time a report arrives has stopped diagnosing.
